text:
ellie: quick follow-up to the model-onboarding rfc — proposing a separate `validator` stage (between ingestion -> bench -> deploy) that enforces contracts and blocks rollouts if checks fail. thoughts?

max: sounds useful. what contracts do you mean exactly?

ellie: minimal set: tokenizer/schema compatibility, kv-cache format, runtime inference shape (input/output names), and performance guardrails (p50/p95, memory). also artifact manifest versioning.

sophia: +1. we should be explicit about units for perf: tokens/sec for throughput, ms for tail latency, peak CPU/GPU mem. otherwise folks ship mismatched expectations.

ellie: agreed. proposal sketch: validator runs on a small dedicated infra (cheap GPU or CPU for quantized models). it runs three checks: 1) smoke (start/forward/backward), 2) compatibility (onnx/torchscript export test, kv-cache), 3) benchmark profile (short-run p50/p95 + mem). failure => block and attach failure logs.

raj: how do we handle large models where running even a short benchmark is costly? can we accept vendor-supplied perf numbers and only run quick shape checks at first?

ellie: yes — define levels: "light" (shape + tokenizer + export) for initial admit, "full" (bench+stress) for production tag. Admit manifest will have `admit_level: light|full`.

lin: we need a manifest contract example. can you paste a minimal schema?

ellie: sure — rough draft:
```
model_manifest_version: 1
name: string
artifact_s3: s3://bucket/path/to/model.tar.gz
framework: pytorch|onnx|tensorRT
tokenizer: s3://.../tokenizer.json
kv_cache_format: lru|kv2
admit_level: light|full
bench_requirements:
  p50_ms: 50
  p95_ms: 200
  max_gpu_mem_mb: 24000
```

maya: minor: include `sample_prompts_s3` and `safety_eval_id` so validator can run deterministic checks and our eval suite.

ellie: good call — will add.

max: how does CI integrate? we don't want this blocking PRs indefinitely.

ellie: CI: validator runs asynchronously on merge to a staging branch. CI status shows: PASS/FAIL/QUEUED. For light admits we allow auto-merge but create a ticket if validator fails. Full admits require explicit engineer sign-off + green validator. `ci-bot` will post status.

ci-bot: note: validator job template created: `validator-light` and `validator-full`. Each run stores artifacts under `s3://redwood-validator/RESULTS/<model-name>/<run-id>/` and attaches logs to the model ticket.

raj: what about runtime-invariant checks like kv-cache binary layout? we must ensure older runtime versions can still load the model.

ellie: add `min_runtime_version` and `compatible_kv_versions` to manifest. validator will run a compatibility shim against recent runtime images.

lin: rollout/gating: if validator passes but bench is close to threshold (say p95 within 10%), can we auto-canary with reduced traffic?

ellie: yes — propose automatic canary policy: `canary_percent` and `canary_duration` in manifest. If bench margin < 15% trigger canary instead of full deploy.

maya: ops question — how do we record historical profiles for regression detection?

ellie: store benchmark fingerprints in our DB (sha of artifact + perf vector). later `regressions-service` will compare new results vs baseline and alert. also tie to `redwood-console` evaluation monitors.

max: who owns maintaining validator infra + test images?
ellie: eng-runtime owns infra + base images. eng-ml owns the validator test suites and bench harness. we'll draft an SLO doc for job latency.

ops-bot: reminder: put security checklist in manifest for private deployments (kms_key_id, data_retention_policy).

ellie: next steps: i'll update the RFC with manifest schema, add example CI workflows, and open a small spike to implement `validator-light`. assigning myself and @max to the spike.

max: ack. i'll pair on the spike next week.

sophia: one more: add a deterministic tokenization test (idempotent roundtrip of input -> tokens -> decode) to prevent subtle token mismatch bugs.

ellie: added. thanks all :tada:
